title: Vision and Mission
content:
About DMU

Dubai Medical University (DMU) embodies the visionary legacy of the late H.E. Saeed Ahmed Lootah, a trailblazer in UAE education. The inception of Dubai Medical College for Girls in 1986 and Dubai Pharmacy College in 1992 attests to his commitment. Recognizing the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and a holistic approach to healthcare education, the transformative merger of these established institutions, along with the addition of the College of Nursing in 2024, marks a significant milestone—the birth of Dubai Medical University. Since its establishment, DMU has continued to expand its academic offerings with the recent addition of the College of Health Sciences in 2026.

This evolution aims to establish a comprehensive healthcare education institution offering a diverse range of programs, from undergraduate to postgraduate degrees, across various healthcare fields. The establishment of DMU not only elevates educational standards but also provides students with a more inclusive and well-rounded learning experience, impacting the healthcare industry in Dubai and the UAE positively.

This preface introduces the exciting journey of quality enhancement undertaken by Dubai Medical University—a journey that reshapes medical, pharmaceutical, and nursing education, envisioning a future where healthcare professionals collaborate seamlessly across disciplines to enhance patient care.

Vision & Mission

The Vision

Empower the next generation of health care leaders.

The Mission

DMU is committed to educate and nurture the next generation of competent health care professionals by providing an excellent learning environment, innovative research, and compassionate patient care to serve humanity.

title: Goals and Objectives
content:
DMU Strategic Goals

  • Goal #1 :To enhance student experience and inspire ethical culture and success.
  • Goal #2 :To promote academic excellence through an innovative learning environment.
  • Goal #3 : To be the leading center of excellence in medical research and education.
  • Goal #4 : To engage in strategic partnership and community outreach.
  • Goal #5 :To enhance development of human capital, professional knowledge, and skills.
  • Goal #6 : To expand health education programs.

DMU mandate

  • To educate and develop highly skilled and compassionate health care professionals who are prepared to meet the needs of patients and the community.
  • To conduct innovative research that advances the knowledge and practice of medicine.
  • To provide high quality patient care in a safe and compassionate environment.
  • To serve the community by providing education, research and clinical services that promote health and wellbeing.
  • To promote awareness and understanding of sustainability and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) across all academic programs and institutional initiatives.

title: VCA Message
content:
It is my great pleasure to welcome you to Dubai Medical University (DMU), a comprehensive medical university in Dubai and one of the fastest-growing medical universities in the UAE.

Operating under the Saeed Ahmed Lootah Foundation, a non-profit charitable organization, DMU holds the distinction of being the first medical college for girls and first pharmacy college for girls in the UAE, established in 1986 and 1992 respectively under the visionary leadership of the late Haji Saeed Lootah. Today, the University stands as a proud reflection of his legacy, an institution built on collaboration, academic excellence, and an unwavering commitment to advancing medical education.

DMU is home to College of Medicine, College of Pharmacy, College of Nursing and College of Health Sciences each dedicated to maintaining the highest standards of education, clinical training, and patient-centered care. As we continue to grow, we plan to introduce new colleges and programs, creating a fully integrated academic health ecosystem where physicians, nurses, pharmacists, and allied health professionals learn and work together to improve patient outcomes. The Dubai Medical University Hospital further enhances our students’ learning experience by providing a dedicated clinical training environment.

Our students are at the heart of everything we do. We are committed to offering world-class facilities, interdisciplinary learning, and research opportunities that empower them to excel. Our experienced faculty and staff form the foundation of our progress, guiding students toward achieving their aspirations while promoting a culture of lifelong learning.

We extend our sincere gratitude to parents for entrusting us with their children’s futures. We honor this responsibility by shaping graduates into ethical, competent, and compassionate healthcare professionals.

Thank you for being part of our journey as we continue to evolve from a respected institution into a world-class medical university. Once again, welcome to DMU. We wish you every success in your academic and professional journey with us.

Prof. Sherief Khalifa

Vice Chancellor – Academic Affairs

title: QAIE Department
content:
About QAIE

The Quality Assurance and Institutional Effectiveness (QAIE) Department at Dubai Medical University (DMU) leads the university’s commitment to continuous quality enhancement. The QAIE Department ensures that all academic programs, administrative units, and institutional services align with national and international standards, promoting excellence in healthcare education, research, and community engagement.

The department is pivotal in strategic planning, operational effectiveness, accreditation, institutional research, and data-informed decision-making, ensuring that DMU delivers high-quality outcomes and maintains a robust quality culture across all its colleges.

QAIE Mission

To foster continuous improvement and excellence in healthcare education and research through evidence-based quality assurance, strategic data utilization, and stakeholder engagement.

title: Accreditation and Ranking
content:
Accreditation & programmes

College of Medicine

Initial Program Accreditation: May 1996 by Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research MOHESR (previous name of MOE).

The program has been regularly re-accredited by the Commission of Academic Accreditation, Ministry of Education.

Following Programs are accredited by Commission for Academic Accreditation (CAA), Ministry of Education, UAE
  • Doctor of Medicine (MD Program)
  • Bachelor in Biomedical Sciences
  • Master of Science in Health Professions Education
  • Postgraduate Diploma in Health Professions Education
  • Master of Global & Digital Public Health Leadership
  • Postgraduate Diploma in Global & Digital Public Health Leadership

Accreditation & programmes

College of Pharmacy

The Bachelor of Pharmacy (BPharm) and Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) degree programs of Dubai Pharmacy College for Girls have been granted International Accreditation by the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE)

Following Programs are accredited by Commission for Academic Accreditation (CAA), Ministry of Education, UAE
  • Bachelor of Pharmacy (BPharm)
    International-Accreditation
  • Master of Pharmacy (MPharm)
  • Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD)
    International-Preaccreditation
  • Master Of Science In Drug Discovery And Development
  • Doctor of Pharmacy (Post-Bachelor)
  • Postgraduate Diploma In Drug Discovery And Development

Accreditation & programmes

College of Nursing

DMU- Bachelor of Science in Nursing Program (BSN) is accredited locally by the Commission for Academic Accreditation (CAA), Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, UAE.

Following Programs are accredited by Commission for Academic Accreditation (CAA), Ministry of Education, UAE
  • Bachelor of Science in Nursing
  • Master of Science in Critical Care Nursing
  • Master of Science in Geriatric Nursing

Accreditation & programmes

College of Health Sciences

Dubai Medical University is dedicated to preparing the next generation of highly skilled healthcare professionals who support modern healthcare systems through advanced clinical practice, technology, and patient-centered care. Building on the Dubai Medical University’s long-standing reputation in medical education, the College combines rigorous academic training with immersive clinical learning to ensure graduates are prepared for the evolving demands of modern healthcare.

Following Programs are accredited by Commission for Academic Accreditation (CAA), Ministry of Education, UAE
  • Bachelor of Science in Anesthesia Technology
  • Bachelor of Science in Audiology and Speech Language Pathology
  • Bachelor of Science in Medical Imaging Sciences
  • Bachelor of Science in Optometry

title: College of Medicine
content:
College of Medicine
COLLEGE OF MEDICINE

Dubai Medical University College of Medicine is committed to providing students with medical education to obtain an accredited degree of Bachelor in Medicine and Surgery in the UAE. The college will achieve its mission by providing a learning environment, both inside and outside the classroom that sustains Islamic values and promotes high levels of student achievement, consistent with the highest standards of academic excellence.

Bachelor, Postgraduate Programs & Courses
Doctor of Medicine(6 Years)Bachelor of Biomedical Science(4 Years)Doctor of Medicine(4 Years)Master of Science in Health Professions Education(2 Years)Master of Global & Digital Public Health Leadership(3 Semesters)PG Diploma in Health Professions Education(1 Years)

PG Diploma in Health Professions Education

(1 Years)

MESSAGE FROM THE DEAN

Dubai Medical University College of Medicine proudly stands as the first private medical college in the UAE to award a degree in Medicine and Surgery. Founded through the vision of Haj Saeed Lootah, the College was established on strong Islamic values to provide women in the UAE the opportunity to pursue medical education locally, empowering them to serve their nation with confidence and purpose.

Today, the College advances that legacy through innovative, future-focused programs delivered within a values-driven academic environment. Our curricula are continuously reviewed and refined in alignment with the best global practices in medical education, ensuring academic excellence and societal relevance.

Beginning Fall 2025, the College introduces a restructured, competency-based 2+4 Doctor of Medicine (MD) curriculum. The first two years focus on general education, followed by two years of integrated biomedical sciences and two years of immersive clinical clerkships.

In addition to the six-year MD track, a Graduate Entry MD (4-year) pathway enables qualified degree holders to enter directly into advanced stages of the program. Uniquely, graduates of health sciences programs may join the MD in Year 3, reinforcing academic mobility and interdisciplinary progression. Both pathways are globally benchmarked and designed to cultivate clinically competent, ethically grounded physicians.

The BBMS program is a forward-looking degree aligned with the UAE Professional Qualification Framework, preparing graduates for national and international certifications. It equips students with scientific expertise, critical thinking, and innovation skills essential for leadership in laboratory medicine, biomedical research, and the broader healthcare and life sciences sectors. The program opens diverse pathways into clinical practice, research, postgraduate education, and healthcare leadership.

To strengthen academic leadership in healthcare, the College offers postgraduate qualifications in Health Professions Education, including a Postgraduate Diploma, and Master’s degree. These programs empower healthcare professionals to excel as educators, curriculum designers, and academic leaders in an evolving global health landscape.

Beyond academics, the College nurtures a vibrant student life. Through an active student union and a wide range of scientific, cultural, social, community, and sports initiatives, students build lifelong professional bonds and meaningful community engagement.

We invite aspiring young women to join College of Medicine, Dubai Medical University, where tradition meets innovation, and education becomes a pathway to service, leadership, and impact.

Prof. Yousif El Tayeb

title: College of Pharmacy
content:
College of Pharmacy
COLLEGE OF PHARMACY

Dubai Medical University’s College of Pharmacy, originally established as Dubai Pharmacy College for Girls (DPCG) in 1992, holds the distinction of being the first pharmacy college in the UAE dedicated exclusively to women. Built on more than three decades of academic excellence, the College continues to nurture future-ready pharmacists who combine scientific knowledge with ethical practice.

The College offers accredited pharmacy programs in Dubai that emphasize pharmaceutical sciences, clinical training, and patient care, ensuring graduates are well-prepared for careers in hospitals, community pharmacies, research, and the pharmaceutical industry. With state-of-the-art laboratories, experienced faculty, and strong industry collaborations, students receive a holistic education that balances innovation with compassion.

As part of Dubai Medical University, the College of Pharmacy carries forward its proud legacy of empowering women in healthcare education while meeting the evolving demands of the global healthcare sector.

Bachelor, Postgraduate Programs & Courses
Bachelor of Pharmacy(4.5 Years)Doctor of Pharmacy – PharmD(6 Years)Doctor of Pharmacy – PharmD Post-Graduate(2 Years)Master of Pharmacy(2 Years)Master of Science in Drug Discovery & Development(2 Years)Postgrad. Diploma in Drug Discovery & Development(1 Years)
MESSAGE FROM THE DEAN

Welcome to the College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University, an institution established by the eminent philanthropist, Hajj Saeed Bin Ahmed Al Lootah, in 1992.

Endowed with the Dubai Appreciation Award in 2004, our University is accredited and licensed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, UAE. The College of Pharmacy has been a pioneer in pharmacy education, with its Bachelor of Pharmacy (BPharm) program receiving international accreditation by the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE) – International Services Program. Today, the College offers a comprehensive range of undergraduate and postgraduate programs, including the Bachelor of Pharmacy (BPharm), Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD), Post-Bachelor Doctor of Pharmacy (Postgraduate PharmD), Master of Pharmacy (MPharm) in Clinical Pharmacy, Master of Science in Drug Discovery & Development (MDD), and the Postgraduate Diploma in Drug Discovery & Development. These programs prepare graduates for advanced professional practice, research, leadership, and academic careers in pharmacy and the pharmaceutical sciences.

In reality, there is no better time to consider Pharmacy as a career than it is today! The pharmacist’s role in healthcare is undergoing continuous evolution and development, and the scope of pharmacy practice has expanded to include pharmacy informatics, vaccination, and independent prescribing, in addition to a plethora of opportunities in the pharmaceutical industry, including Marketing, Medical Affairs, Regulatory Affairs, Pharmacovigilance, Pharmacoeconomics, Pharmaceutical Production, Quality Control, Drug Discovery & Development, and Research.

Today, as part of Dubai Medical University, our College continues to build on its legacy while embracing a future of innovation and excellence. Our students benefit from an integrated academic environment that promotes interprofessional education alongside their peers in the University’s Colleges of Medicine, Dentistry, Nursing, and other health disciplines. This collaborative approach prepares graduates to excel in multidisciplinary healthcare teams and deliver high-quality patient care.

Our partnerships with leading healthcare institutions and internationally acclaimed universities provide opportunities for student and faculty exchange, collaborative research, and academic innovation. Working with globally recognized institutions enhances the quality of our educational programs and ensures that our graduates are equipped to meet the evolving demands of healthcare both regionally and internationally.

Our postgraduate programs, including the Post-Bachelor Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD), Master of Pharmacy (Clinical Pharmacy), and the Master of Science in Drug Discovery & Development (MDD), reflect our commitment to advancing pharmacy education and developing clinical leaders, researchers, and innovators who will shape the future of healthcare.

I invite you to navigate through our website, and even better, visit our campus to meet us in person, interact with our faculty, and explore the endless opportunities we have in store for you at Dubai Medical University, College of Pharmacy.

Prof. Sherief Khalifa

title: College of Nursing
content:
College of Nursing
COLLEGE OF NURSING

College of nursing offers a pathway to a professional career that is both personally fulfilling and in high demand. Nurses are the backbone of the healthcare system, serving as patient advocates, educators, and leaders who blend scientific knowledge with genuine compassion to provide holistic care. The role of a nurse is versatile and extends beyond traditional hospital settings to include public health, education, research, and administration, offering a wide range of career paths and specialization opportunities. The healthcare sector is experiencing significant growth, and the Bureau of Labor Statistics projects a faster-than-average job growth for registered nurses and advanced practice registered nurses, ensuring excellent job security. A nursing education equips you with essential skills like critical thinking, problem-solving, and emotional resilience, which are crucial for success in a dynamic and ever-evolving field. Ultimately, a nursing degree is an investment in a stable career that allows you to make a tangible, positive impact on individuals and communities every day.

The Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) is a premier four-year program embodying the college’s core vision and philosophy. Undergraduates will be awarded the BSN degree upon the successful completion of 120 credit hours.
Key features of the program include:

  • Integrated Core Curriculum: Deep foundational mastery of clinical prerequisites and theoretical healthcare sciences.
  • Elite Clinical Rotations: Real-world training inside Dubai Health hospitals and prominent private medical centers essential for comprehensive skill development.
  • Advanced Medical Education: Hands-on experience utilizing the most sophisticated, state-of-the-art clinical simulation technologies available today.
Bachelor, Master Programs
Bachelor of Science in Nursing(4 Years)Master of Science in Critical Care Nursing(2 Years)Master of Science in Geriatric Nursing(2 Years)

MESSAGE FROM THE DEAN

Welcome to the College of Health Sciences at Dubai Medical University.

Our mission is to educate and inspire the next generation of healthcare professionals who will contribute meaningfully to the advancement of patient care, healthcare systems, and community well-being. At the College of Health Sciences, we believe that excellence in health education requires a strong balance between scientific knowledge, clinical competence, ethical practice, and compassionate care.

One of our greatest strengths is our integration with Dubai Medical University Hospital (DMUH) within the Dubai Medical University Academic Health System. This close collaboration allows our students to benefit from a truly immersive learning environment where academic instruction and clinical practice are closely aligned. Through structured clinical training, advanced laboratories, and exposure to multidisciplinary healthcare teams, students gain the practical experience required to thrive in modern healthcare settings.

As healthcare continues to evolve rapidly, the need for highly skilled allied-health professionals has never been greater. Our college is committed to preparing graduates who are not only technically competent but also innovative, adaptable, and dedicated to improving patient outcomes.

I warmly invite you to explore our college and join us in shaping the future of healthcare.

Prof. Maxime Merheb

title: General Education (GE) at DMU
content:
General Education (GE) at DMU

The General Education (GE) Unit at Dubai Medical University (DMU) provides students with a broad foundation of knowledge, skills, and values that complements their specialized programs. Through carefully designed courses, GE equips students with the competencies necessary to succeed as professionals, leaders, and lifelong learners.

GE enables every DMU graduate to appreciate the social, cultural, ethical, scientific, and global dimensions of health and healthcare. It also strengthens key competencies—including communication, critical thinking, evidence-based practice, digital literacy, quantitative reasoning, teamwork, professionalism, and lifelong learning—that are essential for delivering patient-centered care.

General Education Goals?

The General Education curriculum at Dubai Medical University aims to:

  • Develop well-rounded graduates by fostering lifelong learning, intellectual curiosity, self-awareness, professionalism, and the transferable knowledge, skills, and values required for academic success, professional practice, and responsible citizenship.
  • Promote interdisciplinary learning by integrating knowledge from the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, technology, and health sciences to support holistic, evidence-informed, and patient-centered healthcare.

title: GE Courses & Credit Hours
content:
Current GE Courses & Credit Hours

Course Name Course Code Credit HoursVenue
English Academic Reading & Writing (GER02) 2 CH
Details: This course is designed to help undergraduate students at Dubai Medical University enhance the academic reading and writing skills essential for success in their university studies. The course focuses on developing abilities in reading comprehension, summarization, paraphrasing, essay structure, and research-oriented writing. Students will engage with both general and academic texts and learn how to produce various genres of academic writing, including expository essays. Students will gain skills in critical reading, constructing well-organized paragraphs and essays, and using appropriate academic language in their written work.
Emirati Studies (GER04) 3 CH
Details:The course covers a wide range of topics related to the United Arab Emirates in the contemporary era, focusing on introducing the student to the theoretical and empirical aspects that define political life in the country. It also sheds light on the country’s position in the international arena and its performance in global competitiveness. The course also delves into Emirati society's values, essential heritage, and efforts to develop the Emirati people and foster their contributions to the betterment of the society, emphasizing their crucial role in shaping the country's future. The course also highlights significant achievements in vital national fields, showcasing the UAE’s efforts in furthering human competencies and striving towards the future, the goals of empowering women and achieving development, and the unique features of the UAE’s cultural and literary richness. The course also addresses issues of priority for prudent leadership, including meeting food security requirements and ensuring community safety and prosperity through efforts to enhance community health, improve wellbeing practices, the country’s pioneering pursuits in environmental sustainability, and efforts to achieve technical development and employ its achievements in various fields.
Entrepreneurship, Innovation and Sustainability (GER05) 3 CH
Details:The course “Entrepreneurship, Innovation and Sustainability” has been allotted 3 credit hours which are to be covered over 15 weeks. This course focuses on the concepts and the interconnection between entrepreneurial thinking, innovation and sustainable development. The course is designed in 3 parts to explain the main principles of entrepreneurial process; to link them with concept of innovation and to engage in sustainable development to affect positive societal change. This course will teach students how to think like an entrepreneur and provide the models, tools and frameworks to further develop business or ideas. For future healthcare professionals, this course ensures the ability of decision making to be balanced between professional, ethical approaches on one side, and finance and business on the other side.
Technology in Health (GER06) 2 CH
Details:The course Technology in Health has been allotted 2 credit hours which will be covered over 15 weeks. Before commencing the course, the students should have basic computer skills and English proficiency. This course is designed to provide students with basic information about digital learning and health informatics, and to equip them with the essential skills required as healthcare professionals. The course covers digital innovations and the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare education and training. It also explores the evolution of digital learning education and the web and debates their role in contemporary healthcare education and training. It explores the breadth of technology application, current and emerging trends and showcases both local and international e-health practice and research. The course will stimulate the students to evaluate how e-health can improve the coordination and efficiency of healthcare, and what the barriers might be.
Principles of Psychology (GER07) 2 CH
Details:Principles of Psychology is a foundational course designed for first-year undergraduate students across disciplines. Spanning 14 weeks, the course introduces the scientific study of behavior and mental processes through core areas such as biological bases of behavior, sensation and perception, states of consciousness, learning and memory, cognition, intelligence, motivation, and emotion. Students will explore developmental milestones, personality theories, stress and health psychology, and gain an understanding of psychological disorders through the DSM-5 framework. Emphasis is placed on evidence-based treatment approaches, including psychotherapy and biomedical interventions. The course also integrates elements of social psychology, including group dynamics and clinician-patient interactions. Through lectures, discussions, and applied case studies, students will develop foundational psychological literacy and learn to apply psychological principles to health, wellbeing, and everyday life.
Communication Skills for Interprofessional Practice (GER09) 2 CH (1+1)
Details:This course develops the foundational knowledge and practical communication skills required for effective interprofessional collaboration in healthcare and academic settings. Students explore the principles and processes of human communication while developing competencies in verbal, non-verbal, written, digital, interpersonal, and group communication. Emphasis is placed on communication competence, active listening, self-awareness, intercultural communication, teamwork, conflict management, ethical communication, and professional presentations. Through interactive learning activities, students develop effective communication skills to support collaborative and professional practice across health professions.
Medical Humanities (GER10) 2 CH

Details:Medicine is not only a biological science; it is also shaped by social, cultural, ethical, and human factors. Humanities in Medicine introduces students at the beginning of their medical education to the human and social dimensions of medicine and the complex interactions among patients, healthcare professionals, families, communities, and healthcare systems.
Through literature, narrative medicine, ethics, visual arts, film, patient stories, and reflective practice, students explore the lived experiences of health, illness, suffering, healing, and mortality. The course encourages students to understand patients as individuals with unique stories, values, identities, and cultural contexts rather than as clinical cases alone.
The course provides an early foundation for competencies that will continue to develop throughout the six-year MD program, including ethical reasoning, empathy, professionalism, communication, collaboration, reflective practice, and professional identity formation. When Breath Becomes Air by Paul Kalanithi serves as the principal narrative text, complemented by ethical case discussions, selected films, visual arts, and experiential learning activities.
Students will begin developing an e-portfolio to document their reflections, learning experiences, personal development, and emerging professional identity throughout their medical journey. By integrating scientific knowledge with humanistic understanding, the course promotes patient-centered care, compassion, ethical awareness, professionalism, and respect for human dignity.

Learning in the Modern World (GER11) 2 CH
Details:Learning in the Modern World is a two-credit general education course that introduces BPharm/PharmD students to the skills, habits, and mindsets that will support them throughout their academic and professional journey. Rather than aiming for mastery of any single discipline, the course gives students a broad, practical orientation to topics they are unlikely to encounter explicitly elsewhere in the curriculum: understanding themselves as learners, using evidence-based study strategies, evaluating information critically, engaging responsibly with AI tools, collaborating and communicating with peers and faculty, and learning through experience and community engagement. By the end of the course, students will have a foundational map of the learning, collaboration, and professional-growth skills they will continue developing throughout their pharmacy education and beyond.
Total 18 CH

title: Simulation Centre
content:
DMU Simulation Tour

About Simulation Center

The Simulation Center is currently a functional unit under the Academic Affairs Department, and an active learning resource of Dubai Medical University. The Center officially opened its doors in November 2022. Since then, the Center has offered a wide variety of simulation activities both internally and with external business partners. This state-of-the-art center is keen on training healthcare professionals in a simulated environment with a focus on enhancing patients’ safety and quality of care.

Currently, the simulation center has acquired 4 high-fidelity simulators and 17 task trainers. This inventory covers more than 10 specialties with a large range of basic/advanced clinical skills.

The DMU simulation center has the following members with different roles and responsibilities to ensure effective and efficient operation.

Vision & Mission

Vision

A vision statement is a future-based statement that is a declaration of the Program’s long-term goals. Long-term goals may include a patient improvement benefit. Usually, Programs include the values that will help them to achieve their goal.

Mission

A mission statement is a present-based statement of purpose for the Program, the Program’s reason for existing. The reason usually includes a description of their learners, Program impact, and methods used to make the change (simulation, research, assessment, etc.). The mission statement should guide the actions of the Program and related decision-making.

title: Academic Advising
content:
Academic advising

Students are followed up academically throughout their medical journey in College of Medicine. Each student is assigned an academic advisor that guides her, answers queries, and provides valuable insights and input from their own medical education and clinical experience for our future doctors. Students and advisors are collaborative partners working to achieve the goals and aspirations students set for themselves. Advisors also refer students to different services on campus as needed. Academic advising takes place throughout the years in group and individual settings, advisors report issues students raise and are channeled and actioned accordingly.

At COP, we believe in the importance of addressing our students needs holistically, therefore, a referral system is built to respond to students’ mental health needs where students’ personal, social, and emotional challenges are supported by mental health counselling services on campus. All students’ personal challenges are supported through the counselling independent confidential entity.

title: Hostel Facilities
content:
Hostel Facilities

Hostel facilities are available to students whose families live outside of Dubai. The facility includes single and double occupancy rooms, a study room, a student lounge, a gymnasium, cooking facility with dining area, paid laundry area, and a mosque. Rooms are furnished with all basic amenities. The hostel facility is open for rent to all students and Interns. Cost of rooms for academic year 2025 - 2026 is as follows:

title: Student Council
content:
The Student Council

The Director of Student Affairs, in coordination with Student Engagement and Clubs Specialist and Faculty Club Coordinators, assists and guides in matters pertaining to the Student Council that are consistent with the mission and vision of the University.

The Student Council is a student-run group that dedicates its time and resources to providing the student community with fairness, opportunities, and a voice. The members are elected through a free and secret vote by the students. The Treasurer is an additional post that is recommended by the Director of Student Affairs and approved by Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs.

Coordination Of Student Activities

The Student Council is responsible for:

  • Organizing and arranging national and international events.
  • Proposing functions, special occasions, and activities for students.
  • Assisting in official DMU events such as New Student Orientation, DMU Iftar, and DMU Global Day.
  • Organizing educational and recreational trips at least once per semester.

Conduct of Student Activities

  • Organizing educational, scientific, cultural, sports, and sustainability events, initiatives, and competitions.
  • Hosting talks on health-related topics.
  • Announcing activities and highlights through official DMU platforms (Instagram and the website) only after approval from the Director of Student Affairs.
  • Promoting diversity, inclusion, and student engagement in all events.

Student Council Elections Procedure

  • Elections are held at the beginning of the second semester each academic year.
  • The Student Engagement and Clubs Specialist and Faculty Club Coordinators oversee the election process, announcements, and candidate registration.
  • Students may run for one position only; Year 1 students are encouraged to run for Vice President or Assistant General Secretary.
  • Campaigns are supervised by the Elections Organizing Team (EOT), under the guidance of the Student Engagement and Clubs Specialist and Faculty Club Coordinators.
  • Voting is conducted through Microsoft Forms during the Elections Ceremony, following candidate speeches.
  • Results are announced through official DMU communication channels following approval by the Director of Student Affairs and the Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs.
  • Each Student Council term is one academic year.

title: Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI)
content:
Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI)

Dubai Medical University (DMU) is fundamentally committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse, and equitable community for all its stakeholders. The university’s mission is dedicated to driving a quality culture and structure that ensures diversity, equality & inclusion. DMU actively promotes the UAE values of tolerance and acceptance across the campus environment through various initiatives and awareness campaigns.

The institutional commitment ensures that all employees and stakeholders adhere to core values of fairness and equitable treatment, inclusiveness, collegiality, respect, integrity, honesty, and ethical behavior.

Diversity and Equality for Students

DMU ensures that all students have the right to a safe and inclusive learning environment. This commitment is formalized through specific departments dedicated to student welfare and success.

Institutional Responsibility

The mandate for promoting diversity and inclusion among students belongs to the Deanship of Student Affairs (DSA) and the elected Student Council. Deanship of Student Affairs (DSA) Role: The DSA is specifically tasked with promoting diversity and inclusion initiatives and creating a welcoming and inclusive campus environment for students from all backgrounds. Student Voice and Representation: The elected Student Council, which operates under the coordination of the DSA, plays a key role in supporting this mission by actively promoting Diversity and Inclusion and fostering an environment that provides equal opportunities for all students.

Core Principles of Student Equity

  • Equal Opportunity in student admission:
    • DMU operates as an equal opportunity institution that will not distinguish between race, religion, or gender when admitting and formulating an offer to an applicant.
  • Freedom from Discrimination and Harassment:
    • Students are legally entitled to respect in an educational environment which is free from threat, harassment, abuse, or discrimination.
    • DMU strictly prohibits discrimination, non-tolerance, and hate speech.
    • Any student misconduct that compromises academic integrity or community standards, including harassment or bullying, is subject to disciplinary action.
  • Support for Students of Determination (SOD):
    • DMU operates as an inclusive community committed to addressing the educational needs of its Students of Determination (SOD) on campus.
    • Students requiring support must submit an official medical report of their diagnosis.
    • Appropriate accommodation is provided on campus depending on the students’ educational needs to support them in achieving their goals.
  • Holistic Wellbeing:
    • The DSA provides holistic support focusing on students’ physical, mental and emotional wellbeing. This support is aimed at responding to the needs of the comprehensive student population.
Diversity and Equality for Faculty and Staff

DMU is committed to maintaining transparency, fairness, and equality across all employment and administrative practices.

Institutional Responsibility

The responsibility for ensuring diversity, equity, and inclusion for faculty and staff belongs to the Human Resources (HR) Unit. DMU’s comprehensive Policy on Disability, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion applies to all job applicants and employees (including faculty, staff, researchers, and professional staff). The purpose of this HR-led policy is to create an environment that is inclusive, diverse, and equitable for all employees.

Core Principles of Faculty and Staff Equity

  • Equal Opportunity in Recruitment and Hiring:
    • DMU operates as an equal opportunity institution that will not distinguish between race, religion, or gender when selecting and formulating an offer to a candidate.
    • Recruitment procedures aim to promote good practice that ensures consistency, fairness, and equality in all recruitment-related matters.
    • There must be no discrimination against any employee or job applicant based on their disability, race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.
  • Equal Pay and Compensation:
    • DMU adheres to the UAE Cabinet Law of 2018 specifying equal wages and salaries for women and men who perform the same work or work of equal value.
    • Compensation is determined based on education, experience, skills, character, and position requirements.
  • Inclusive Work Environment and Conduct:
    • Faculty members are expected to promote and maintain a culture of equality and diversity.
    • All faculty and staff are expected to treat their colleagues with dignity and respect and maintain an environment free from discrimination, and harassment.
    • The DMU Code of Conduct strictly prohibits harassment, offensive behaviors, or discrimination based on protected characteristics.
  • Disability and Accommodation
    • The university is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to all employees of DMU with disabilities to enable them to perform their job duties. This may involve modifications to the work environment, job duties, or work schedule.
  • Inclusive Professional Development
    • DMU emphasizes that the importance of diversity and inclusivity must be emphasized in all professional development events.
    • Events must be accessible to all participants regardless of their background, gender, or socio-economic status, and speaker diversity must be considered.

title: Bachelor of Science in Anesthesia Technology
display_title: BACHELOR OF SCIENCE IN ANESTHESIA TECHNOLOGY
content:
Apply Now

Program Overview

The Bachelor of Science in Anesthesia Technology (BS-ANTech) at Dubai Medical University is a four-year program designed to prepare highly skilled perioperative professionals who support anesthesia delivery, patient monitoring, and surgical safety. The curriculum combines strong foundations in biomedical sciences with specialized training in anesthesia systems, patient care technologies, and clinical practice in modern healthcare environments.

During the first two years, students build essential knowledge in anatomy, physiology, microbiology, pharmacology, and pathology, while developing professional competencies in communication, research, and healthcare ethics. Early exposure to perioperative care, sterility science, infection control, and anesthesia technology introduces students to the clinical environment.

In Year 3, the program advances into specialized anesthesia topics including patient monitoring, anesthesia equipment and safety systems, perioperative diagnostics, and anesthesia management across different surgical contexts. Simulation and laboratory training strengthen clinical decision-making and teamwork.

The final year focuses on advanced anesthesia practice and extensive supervised clinical training in operating rooms and perioperative units. Through these experiences, graduates develop the technical competence, critical thinking, and professional confidence needed to contribute effectively to multidisciplinary surgical teams and to support high standards of patient safety and care.

Program Overview

The Bachelor of Science in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (BS-ASLP) at Dubai Medical University is a four-year program designed to prepare professionals capable of assessing, diagnosing, and supporting individuals with speech, language, hearing, and swallowing disorders across the lifespan. The program integrates biomedical sciences, communication sciences, and clinical training to develop graduates who can contribute effectively to multidisciplinary healthcare and rehabilitation teams.

During the first two years, students build a strong scientific and academic foundation through courses in biology, chemistry, physics, anatomy and physiology, microbiology, pharmacology, pathology, and research methods. Students are introduced to the fundamentals of communication disorders, linguistics and phonetics, psychology, and language development, providing the essential knowledge required to understand speech, hearing, and human communication.

In Year 3, the curriculum progresses to specialized topics in speech-language pathology and audiology, including neuroscience of communication, voice and fluency disorders, motor speech disorders, school-age language disorders, bilingualism, hearing assessment, pediatric audiology, auditory processing disorders, and swallowing disorders. Laboratory sessions and applied training strengthen diagnostic and clinical reasoning skills.

The final year focuses on intensive supervised clinical practicum in both speech-language pathology and audiology, allowing students to apply assessment and intervention techniques in real clinical settings. The program concludes with a research project that develops analytical and evidence-based practice skills, preparing graduates for professional practice and further specialization in communication health sciences.

Program Overview

The Bachelor of Science in Optometry (BS-OPT) at Dubai Medical University is a four-year program designed to prepare primary eye-care professionals capable of examining vision, detecting ocular disorders, and supporting the prevention and management of visual impairment. The program integrates strong foundations in biomedical sciences with specialized training in optical science, vision assessment, ocular health, and clinical optometric practice.

During the first two years, students build essential knowledge in biology, chemistry, physics, anatomy and physiology, microbiology, and pharmacology, while developing professional competencies in communication, research, and healthcare ethics. Students are introduced to the fundamentals of optometry, including geometrical and visual optics, ocular anatomy and physiology, and the principles of optometric examination and binocular vision. Laboratory sessions provide hands-on training in visual optics and basic clinical assessment techniques.

In Year 3, the curriculum advances into specialized optometric topics such as ophthalmic lenses and dispensing, diagnostic instrumentation, ocular diseases, ocular pharmacology, visual perception, and optometric care across different age groups. Practical laboratories strengthen students’ clinical examination skills and their ability to use diagnostic equipment and vision assessment technologies.

The final year focuses on advanced optometric practice and extensive supervised clinical training in eye-care clinics and healthcare settings. Students also study areas such as contact lenses, community eye care, myopia management, and low-vision rehabilitation. Through these experiences, graduates develop the technical competence, clinical reasoning, and professional confidence required to deliver high-quality vision care and contribute to multidisciplinary healthcare teams.

BPharm Program Overview

The Bachelor of Pharmacy program at Dubai Medical University spans four and half years with 160 credit hours. It combines foundational sciences, pharmaceutical studies, professional skills, and experiential practice.

Years 1–2 build a base in biomedical sciences: anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, microbiology, and pharmaceutics. General education in communication, technology, psychology, and culture is integrated. Early exposure to pharmacy includes law, ethics, and public health. Laboratory sessions reinforce theoretical knowledge with practical skills.

By Year 2, students complete Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience I in community pharmacies.

Years 3–4 focus on integrated pharmacotherapy modules blending pathophysiology, pharmacology, chemistry, and therapy. Supporting subjects include pharmacokinetics, pharmacoeconomics, pharmacovigilance, genetics, and immunology. Case-based learning and simulations enhance decision-making and teamwork skills. Hospital-based IPPE II follows in Year 3. Electives allow exploration of specialized pharmacy or science topics. Graduates emerge as competent pharmacists, prepared for licensure and diverse healthcare, academic, regulatory, or industry roles.

The program responds to the growing demand for nurses with specialized expertise in complex and rapidly changing physiological conditions, advanced patient assessment, clinical decision-making, life-support technologies, and coordinated care across high-acuity healthcare environments.

The curriculum integrates advanced health assessment, pathophysiology, clinical pharmacology, critical care nursing theory, evidence-based practice, and research. Students complete 400 supervised clinical hours across two critical care nursing practicum courses, enabling them to apply advanced clinical reasoning, respond to acute and life-threatening conditions, collaborate effectively with interprofessional teams, and support patients and families throughout complex critical illness.

Research preparation is embedded throughout the program through advanced research methods, data management and analysis, and a master’s thesis. Graduates will be equipped to improve the quality and safety of critical care, lead practice-development and quality-improvement initiatives, contribute to healthcare policy and professional education, and advance nursing scholarship in the UAE and the wider region.

title: College Of Medicine About
content:
About College Of Medicine

More than 30 years ago, establishing a world-renowned medical education institution for girls in the UAE would seem like an impossible dream. Yet, on August 1, 1986, our founder Haj Saeed bin Ahmed Al Lootah accomplished that very goal and classes began at DMU College of Medicine with Professor Dr. Zahira H. Abdin as the founding dean. His visionary dream had become a reality.

During these formative years, the College received substantial professional support and advice from the Leicester Medical School in the United Kingdom and the Cairo Medical School in Egypt. This international contribution combined with the faculty's extensive experience led to the creation of an intensive curriculum that would incorporate the best of the world's medical practices.

Since its inception, College of Medicine has been fortunate to receive help from the government of Dubai's Department of Health and Medical Services under its former Director H.E. Dr. Juma Khalfan Balhoul. The departments hospitals opened their doors and welcomed College of Medicine (COM) students for clinical training. Our continued drive for excellence demands seamless integration between clinical and pre-clinical phases. In 2004, a Memorandum of Understanding was signed by DHA and COM to secure this process.

What we now know, as an outstanding educational institution, is a product of the cooperative solidarity of a group of people who put their heart and soul into it. Three decades of academic distinction have made College of Medicine a truly dynamic center of higher education par excellence.

With over 1500 graduates practicing medicine across the world and a campus that includes professors and students from over 50 different countries, DMCG has earned a reputation as one of the best institutions for medical education and a beacon of academic excellence.

In September 2022, the College ownership was transferred under "Saeed Ahmad Lootah Charity Foundation".

title: Goals and Objectives
content:
Goals and Objectives

The College’s goals are grounded in Islamic values that promote faith, knowledge, ethical conduct, service, responsibility, respect to all regardless of faith or race. Guided by the Qur’anic principle that human life has a purposeful relationship with the Creator, the College seeks to integrate academic excellence with integrity, compassion, and service to society.
Through its educational, research, and community activities, the College aims to develop competent professionals and responsible global citizens who contribute meaningfully to healthcare and human well-being.

  • Goal #1 :Enhance the Student Experience and Foster a Culture of Success.
    Provide an inclusive, supportive, and inspiring learning environment that promotes academic achievement, personal development, well-being, leadership, entrepreneurship, and global citizenship in accordance with Islamic values.
  • Goal #2 :Contribute to the Knowledge Economy.
    Offer high-quality, internationally benchmarked academic programs and assessment practices that support intellectual growth, professional competence, lifelong learning, and meaningful contributions to society.
  • Goal #3 : Advance Research and Innovation.
    Promote high-quality, ethical, and impactful research in clinical practice, biomedical and pharmaceutical sciences, life sciences, health professions education, public health, and healthcare management. Research activities will address relevant health and societal challenges and support evidence-informed solutions at national and international levels.
  • Goal #4 :Develop Human Capital.
    Recruit, develop, and retain qualified faculty and staff who are committed to excellence, innovation, and continuous professional development. Attract capable national and international students and graduates who contribute to the College’s academic reputation and institutional identity.
  • Goal #5 :Serve the Community.
    Respond to community and healthcare needs through education, research, clinical engagement, professional development, and social responsibility. Contribute to the educational, cultural, economic, and health development of the UAE, the region, and the wider global community.
  • Goal #6 : Strengthen Partnerships and Engagement.
    Build sustainable partnerships with healthcare institutions, academic organizations, government entities, industry, and community stakeholders. These collaborations will support education, research, innovation, workforce development, and improved health outcomes.

title: Dean Message
content:
Message from the Dean

The College of Medicine at Dubai Medical University proudly stands as the first private medical college in the United Arab Emirates to award a degree in Medicine and Surgery. Established through the vision of Haj Saeed Lootah, the College was founded on strong Islamic values and a commitment to providing women in the UAE with the opportunity to pursue medical education locally. This pioneering vision has empowered generations of graduates to serve their communities and nation with knowledge, confidence, compassion, and purpose.

Today, the College continues to build on this distinguished legacy by offering innovative, future-focused academic programs within a values-driven and supportive learning environment. Its curricula are continuously reviewed and enhanced in alignment with international standards and best practices in medical and health professions education. This ensures that all programs remain academically rigorous, professionally relevant, and responsive to the evolving needs of healthcare systems and society.

Beginning in Fall 2025, the College introduces a restructured, competency-based 2+4 Doctor of Medicine curriculum. The first two years focus on general education and the development of foundational knowledge, communication skills, critical thinking, and professional attributes. These are followed by two years of integrated biomedical and clinical sciences and two years of immersive clinical clerkships. Through this progressive structure, students develop the knowledge, skills, behaviours, and clinical competencies required for safe, ethical, compassionate, and patient-centred medical practice.

In addition to the six-year Doctor of Medicine pathway, the College offers a four-year Graduate Entry Doctor of Medicine pathway for qualified degree holders. This pathway enables eligible applicants to enter directly into the advanced stages of medical education. Graduates of relevant health sciences programs may also be eligible to join the Doctor of Medicine program in Year 3, promoting academic mobility, interdisciplinary progression, and flexible entry into the medical profession. Both pathways are globally benchmarked and designed to prepare clinically competent, scientifically informed, ethically grounded, and socially accountable physicians.

The Bachelor of Biomedical Sciences is a forward-looking undergraduate degree aligned with the UAE Professional Qualification Framework. The program equips students with a strong foundation in biomedical sciences, laboratory practice, scientific inquiry, critical thinking, research, innovation, and problem-solving. It prepares graduates for national and international professional certifications and opens diverse career pathways in laboratory medicine, biomedical research, biotechnology, diagnostics, healthcare, and the wider life sciences sector. Graduates may also pursue postgraduate education, research careers, entrepreneurship, and leadership roles across healthcare and scientific institutions.

To strengthen educational excellence and academic leadership within the healthcare professions, the College offers postgraduate qualifications in health professions education, including the Postgraduate Diploma in Health Professions Education and the Master of Science in Health Professions Education. These programs are designed for healthcare professionals seeking to advance their roles as educators, curriculum developers, assessment specialists, educational researchers, mentors, and academic leaders. Through the integration of contemporary educational theory, evidence-based teaching, curriculum design, assessment, leadership, and scholarship, graduates are prepared to enhance the quality of education and professional development across healthcare institutions.

The College also offers the Postgraduate Diploma in Global & Digital Public Health Leadership and the Master of Global & Digital Public Health Leadership. These innovative postgraduate programs prepare professionals to respond to complex public health challenges in an increasingly interconnected, data-driven, and digitally enabled world.

The programs integrate global health, public health leadership, digital transformation, health technologies, health informatics, data-informed decision-making, policy development, strategic management, innovation, and health systems strengthening. The Postgraduate Diploma provides a focused and professionally relevant foundation for individuals seeking to strengthen their knowledge and leadership capabilities in global and digital public health. The master’s degree offers advanced academic and professional preparation for strategic, research-informed, and senior leadership roles.

Graduates of these programs are equipped to lead public health initiatives, influence health policy, manage digital health transformation, apply emerging technologies responsibly, and support the development of resilient, equitable, sustainable, and responsive health systems at national, regional, and international levels.

Beyond academic excellence, the College is committed to nurturing a vibrant, inclusive, and engaging student experience. Through an active student union and a wide range of scientific, cultural, social, community service, leadership, and sports initiatives, students develop valuable personal and professional skills, build lifelong relationships, and contribute meaningfully to the wider community.

The College also promotes a culture of professionalism, innovation, collaboration, social responsibility, and lifelong learning. Students are encouraged to participate in research, community engagement, interdisciplinary activities, and leadership opportunities that enrich their educational journey and prepare them to make a positive impact in healthcare and society.

We invite aspiring students, healthcare professionals, educators, researchers, and future leaders to join the College of Medicine at Dubai Medical University, where tradition meets innovation and education becomes a transformative pathway to service, discovery, professional excellence, leadership, and lasting societal impact.


Dean, College of Medicine

Prof. Yousif El Tayeb
Dean, College of Medicine

Program Overview

The Postgraduate Diploma in Global & Digital Public Health Leadership (GDPHL) prepares the next generation of public health leaders capable of designing, implementing, and evaluating resilient and digitally enabled health systems.

The program integrates four critical domains of modern public health leadership:

  • Healthcare leadership and governance
  • Global health systems and policy
  • Humanitarian action and disaster medicine
  • Artificial intelligence and digital public health

Graduates will gain the strategic, technical, and leadership competencies required to address complex global health challenges, strengthen health system resilience, and leverage digital technologies for population health improvement.

The program also includes applied internship experience and research training, allowing students to work on real-world public health leadership challenges in government, healthcare systems, humanitarian organizations, and digital health ecosystems.

title: Master of Global & Digital Public Health Leadership Admission
display_title: Master of Global & Digital Public Health Leadership Admission
content:
Master of Global & Digital Public Health Leadership Admission

Admission Requirements (Master/Diploma) Program

1. Standard admission (recommended)

    • Academic: Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field (health sciences, public health, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, allied health, health administration, informatics, data/CS, social sciences with health focus).
    • Minimum GPA: e.g., 3/4.0 or equivalent (institutional policy can set threshold).
    • For non-GPA grading systems, please obtain a course-by-course evaluation from an Educational Credential Evaluators (ECE) or http://www.ece.org or World Education Services (WES) https://www.wes.org/
    • For degrees obtained outside the UAE, please obtain ECE - http://www.ece.orgor WEShttps://www.wes.org/
    • Experience: Preferably ≥ 1–2 years relevant work experience (health sector, NGO, government, digital health, analytics, emergency response).

All prospective applicants seeking admission must undergo the process of obtaining equivalency/recognition for their educational degrees through the UAE Ministry of Education. The attestation procedure varies depending on whether the degree was earned within or outside the UAE. Details regarding the Equivalency/Recognition requirements for certificates obtained within or outside the UAE can be accessed through the Ministry of Education https://www.moe.gov.ae/En/EServices/Pages/ServiceCatalog.aspx.

  • Master and PhD Holders are exempted from providing GPA requirements

Conditional Admission:

Graduate with a minimum cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 2.5 to 2.9 on a 4.0 scale or its established equivalent shall be conditionally admitted to the first semester as follows:

  • Is allowed to take a maximum of nine credit hours of courses studied for the graduate program during the period of conditional admission, and
  • Must achieve a minimum CGPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, or its established equivalent, in these nine credits of courses studied for the graduate program to progress to the second semester or be subject to dismissal.

Graduate with a minimum cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 2.0 to 2.49 on a 4.0 scale or its established equivalent shall be admitted to the first semester as follows:

  • Is required to successfully complete a maximum of nine graduate-level credit hours as remedial preparation for the graduate program. These remedial courses are not for credit within the degree program.
  • Must achieve a minimum CGPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, or its established equivalent, in these nine credits of remedial courses in order to be admitted to the graduate program or be subject to dismissal.

2. Professional Experience:

  • At least one year of professional experience in health professions education, clinical practice, academic teaching, or administration in a healthcare or educational institution.
  • Preference is given to applicants currently involved in teaching or training in health professions education

3. English Language Proficiency

    • IELTS score of 6.0 or above, or
    • TOEFL iBT score of 79 or above, or
  • Exemption from English proficiency requirement may be granted if prior education was in English, a letter for Language of Instruction is required. Additionally, all Master & PhD holders are not required to submit English proficiency.

4. Personal Statement:

  • A written statement (500–750 words) outlining the applicants:
    • Motivation for pursuing the MHPE program.
    • Career goals in health professions education.
    • Relevant experience and how the program aligns with their professional development.

5. Letters of Recommendation

A letter of recommendation from academic or professional supervisors, attesting to the applicants:

  • Academic capability
  • Professional commitment
  • Suitability for graduate study in education

6. Curriculum Vitae (CV)

    • A current CV detailing academic background, work experience, professional activities, & achievements.

7. Interview

Shortlisted candidates may be invited for a personal or virtual interview to assess:

  • Communication skills
  • Commitment to health professions education
  • Alignment with the program’s objectives

Refund Policy of Tuition Fees

Refund applies as follows:

  • A 5% deduction is applicable on the full tuition fees if the candidate applies for withdrawal before the beginning of the academic year.
  • A 25% deduction is applicable on the full tuition fees if the candidate applies for withdrawal during the first 10 working days of the academic year.
  • A 50% deduction is applicable on the full tuition fees if the candidate applies for withdrawal after 10 working days of the academic year.
  • If a student withdraws after the second semester start, no refund is granted at all.
  • In case of unforeseen circumstances, refund may only be accepted after Deans’ Council review based on student request supported with evidence.
  • Hostel and Transportation fees are refunded based on pro rata on a full monthly basis, not per day. (Month fraction is considered as a full month).
  • Refund requests for the above valid reasons should be made through the Student Affairs Department in collaboration with Accounts Department through a written request along with the original fee receipt. Refunds will be made after clearance of dues, if any. Refunds will be credited by bank transfer or Cheque to the same payer (student’s parent / guardian / sponsor) bank account and not given in cash.

The following are non-refundable:

  • Visa fee
  • Application fee
  • Transport fee
  • Seat Reservation fee.
  • Full tuition fee in case of dismissal/suspension for disciplinary reasons
Scholarship and Discounts

DMU is keen to attract talented students and support their educational journey, as such we will offer Merit Scholarship to students as per criteria published Merit is based on academic performance.

Merit is based on academic performance.

For the MD program:

  • For new students, the top five ranked students applying (based on admission placement exam and Multiple Mini Interview score) will be granted 20% merit scholarship on their annual fees.
  • For continuing students, the top five students as per end of academic year Cumulative GPA are given the Merit Scholarship.

For other Programs:

  • For new students, the details of the merit discount are published on DMU website on annual basis.
  • For continuing students, the top five students are granted the Merit Scholarship of 20% discount on the semester fees as per end of semester Cumulative GPA.
External Scholarships

Students can also be enrolled at DMU and receive external scholarships and this cannot be combined with any DMU internal scholarship or discounts. Sponsoring entities would pay the students fees and other expenses as per their agreement with the student. Students or sponsor are required to provide DMU Admission and Registration Department and Finance Department a written confirmation of the sponsorship or scholarship letter or agreement with the student. DMU is required to provide the sponsor with student transcripts, attendance records and invoices directly without prior notice to the student. If a student loses a scholarship, they are required to pay all pending fees to DMU.

Discounts

Siblings Discount
Siblings enrolled at DMU are eligible for a 10% discount on tuition fee only and this is applicable for the second student that joins the program and 15% for the third. Once the first student graduates the discount ceases and the student pay the whole tuition fee. This is not applicable for transportation or hostel fees.

DMU Graduates:
All graduates of DMU are eligible for a 20% tuition fee discount on postgraduate programs offered.

  • Employee’s discount
    • All DMU full-time faculty and staff are eligible for a 75% tuition fee discount on postgraduate diploma and Master of Health Professions Education Program offered at DMU.
    • All DMU adjunct faculty are eligible for a 50% tuition fee discount on postgraduate diploma and Master of Health Professions Education Program offered at DMU.
    • Children of DMU faculty, staff and adjunct faculty are eligible for a 15% discount on Tuition annual fees.
  • International applicants
    • All international applicants are eligible for a 50% tuition fee discount on postgraduate diploma and Master of Health Professions Education Program offered at DMU . International applicants' discounts are for the first two cohorts joining the program.

title: About the College of Pharmacy
content:
About the College of Pharmacy

Established in 1992 under the guidance of the visionary leader, Haj Saeed Bin Ahmed Al Lootah, Dubai Medical University, College of Pharmacy (DMU COP) is dedicated to offering accredited pharmacy education at both undergraduate and graduate levels to female students. Our commitment lies in imparting values-based education, advancing Pharmacy knowledge through research, and engaging in community service to benefit the pharmacy profession, scientific community, and the public.

With a diverse student body representing over 30 countries worldwide, our programs are accredited by the Commission for Academic Accreditation (CAA), Ministry of Education, UAE. At DMU COP, we provide a nurturing environment for a well-rounded education, facilitated by highly qualified faculty from diverse backgrounds.

title: Dean's Message
content:
Message from the Dean

Welcome to the College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University, an institution established by the eminent philanthropist, Hajj Saeed Bin Ahmed Al Lootah, in 1992.

Endowed with the Dubai Appreciation Award in 2004, our University is accredited and licensed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, UAE. The College of Pharmacy has been a pioneer in pharmacy education, with its Bachelor of Pharmacy (BPharm) program receiving international accreditation by the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE) – International Services Program. Today, the College offers a comprehensive range of undergraduate and postgraduate programs, including the Bachelor of Pharmacy (BPharm), Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD), Post-Bachelor Doctor of Pharmacy (Postgraduate PharmD), Master of Pharmacy (MPharm) in Clinical Pharmacy, Master of Science in Drug Discovery & Development (MDD), and the Postgraduate Diploma in Drug Discovery & Development. These programs prepare graduates for advanced professional practice, research, leadership, and academic careers in pharmacy and the pharmaceutical sciences.

In reality, there is no better time to consider Pharmacy as a career than it is today! The pharmacist’s role in healthcare is undergoing continuous evolution and development, and the scope of pharmacy practice has expanded to include pharmacy informatics, vaccination, and independent prescribing, in addition to a plethora of opportunities in the pharmaceutical industry, including Marketing, Medical Affairs, Regulatory Affairs, Pharmacovigilance, Pharmacoeconomics, Pharmaceutical Production, Quality Control, Drug Discovery & Development, and Research.

Today, as part of Dubai Medical University, our College continues to build on its legacy while embracing a future of innovation and excellence. Our students benefit from an integrated academic environment that promotes interprofessional education alongside their peers in the University’s Colleges of Medicine, Dentistry, Nursing, and other health disciplines. This collaborative approach prepares graduates to excel in multidisciplinary healthcare teams and deliver high-quality patient care.

Our partnerships with leading healthcare institutions and internationally acclaimed universities provide opportunities for student and faculty exchange, collaborative research, and academic innovation. Working with globally recognized institutions enhances the quality of our educational programs and ensures that our graduates are equipped to meet the evolving demands of healthcare both regionally and internationally.

Our postgraduate programs, including the Post-Bachelor Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD), Master of Pharmacy (Clinical Pharmacy), and the Master of Science in Drug Discovery & Development (MDD), reflect our commitment to advancing pharmacy education and developing clinical leaders, researchers, and innovators who will shape the future of healthcare.

I invite you to navigate through our website, and even better, visit our campus to meet us in person, interact with our faculty, and explore the endless opportunities we have in store for you at Dubai Medical University, College of Pharmacy.


Dean, College of Pharmacy

Prof. Sherief Khalifa
Dean, College of Pharmacy

Student Success Center

The Student Success Center (SSC) at the College of Pharmacy is dedicated to supporting students throughout their academic journey and fostering their personal and professional development. As a central hub for student support, the SSC provides a welcoming environment where students can seek guidance on academic, personal, and university-related matters.

The SSC works proactively to promote student success by monitoring attendance and academic progress, identifying students who may benefit from additional support, and collaborating closely with faculty members, academic departments, and university services. Through timely interventions, personalized guidance, and student-centered initiatives, the SSC helps students overcome challenges, remain engaged in their studies, and achieve their full potential.

Committed to promoting student well-being, academic excellence, and a positive learning environment, the SSC provides a range of services that enhance students' overall learning experience.

Services provided:

    • Mentorship
    • Peer Tutoring (LEAP)
    • Student Attendance Monitoring
    • Grievances, Appeals and Suggestions
    • Academic Integrity and Student Conduct
    • Career Guidance

    Academic mentorship is an integral part of our student support system, providing students with continuous academic guidance, personalized support, and encouragement throughout their studies.

    Every student is assigned a faculty mentor to provide ongoing academic guidance and support. Faculty mentors meet regularly with students to discuss academic performance, assist with academic planning, monitor academic progress, help them set academic and professional goals, and address any personal or academic challenges that may affect their success. They also support students in adjusting to university life, making informed academic decisions, understanding university requirements, and accessing appropriate university resources when needed.

    The Student Success Center works closely with students, faculty mentors, and the Associate Dean for Academic Affairs to identify challenges and develop effective strategies for academic success. Through continuous mentoring, personalized support, early intervention, and collaborative support, the SSC and faculty mentors help students stay on track, achieve their academic goals, and make the most of their university experience.

    The Learning Enhancement and Peer Support (LEAP) Program is a structured, student-led peer tutoring initiative at the COP. LEAP fosters a collaborative and inclusive learning environment where students support one another in strengthening their understanding of course material, developing effective study strategies, and building confidence in their learning.

    LEAP tutors are selected through a structured, merit-based process and receive formal training in effective tutoring practices, communication skills, learning strategies, professionalism, and academic integrity before supporting their peers. Working under faculty supervision, they provide high-quality academic support while promoting ethical and collaborative learning.

    The program offers a variety of learning formats, including one-to-one tutoring, small-group tutoring, study sessions, and workshops. Through LEAP, students receive guidance from trained peer tutors who help reinforce key concepts, improve study habits, develop critical thinking skills, and enhance overall academic success. At the same time, the program provides peer tutors with valuable opportunities to develop leadership, communication, teaching, and professional skills.

    The SSC manages student attendance records and reviews absence excuses in learning and assessment sessions, in accordance with university policies. By maintaining accurate records, the SSC helps students stay on track with their studies and ensures transparency in attendance monitoring.

    Attendance alerts are issued regularly to students whose attendance falls below the required threshold, and faculty mentors are informed to facilitate timely follow-up, guidance, and support.
